label: epa-vs-statbotics
rationale: SC-2 (quick task 260904-4aa): tolerance bands for scripts/epaVsStatbotics.ts --check, built from the offseason-inclusive, full-range (2022-2026) run's min-matches(>=12) arm — matching packages/harness/epaStatboticsCompare.ts's compareSeason output and production's own publish:seasons stream composition (includeOffseason: true). The min-matches arm (not the all-teams arm) is the gated one: low-match teams are noisy on both sides and would otherwise dominate meanAbsoluteDifference (see docs/models/epa-vs-statbotics.md). Bands are centred on the measured value: ordinaryLeastSquaresSlope/pearson at +/-0.05, meanAbsoluteDifference at +/-1.0 points, and both standard deviations at +/-max(1.5, 10% of the measured value) so a season with a much larger point scale (2026: ourSD ~51) is not gated by an absolute band sized for a smaller-scale season (2022: ourSD ~10). This corpus/EPA computation is deterministic (no randomness in the aggregate statistics), so re-running scripts/epaVsStatbotics.ts unchanged reproduces these figures exactly -- the bands exist to catch a REAL regression in EPA's attribution arithmetic or component extraction, not day-to-day measurement noise. The 2026 season is still in progress as of this baseline's creation date; its own row will need re-measuring (and likely widening or replacing) as more of that season is played and both our own EPA state and Statbotics' team-year figures shift with it -- this is a known, named limitation of gating a live season, not an oversight.
